evidence.rationale: Unique passwords reduce credential reuse across systems and accounts, limiting adversary use of one compromised password to pivot through valid accounts.
Unique passwords reduce adversary use of default or vendor-provided account credentials.
Domain accounts can span users, admins, and services; unique passwords reduce domain credential reuse and lateral reuse risk.
Unique local passwords reduce reuse of one compromised local account credential across multiple endpoints or servers.
Unique passwords reduce cloud/SaaS credential overlap and lateral reuse risk

Unique passwords and minimum password lengths, which directly reduce the effectiveness of brute-force attacks by increasing the number of possible password combinations and limiting the reuse of compromised credentials across systems. This makes online password guessing and offline password cracking more difficult and reduces the success of credential-stuffing attacks.
Enforced minimum password length increases the search space and reduces the effectiveness of password guessing.
Longer passwords materially increase the effort required to recover plaintext passwords from captured hashes or related material.
Unique, non-common passwords reduce success of spraying common passwords across many accounts.
This directly counters password overlap from breached credentials reused across personal, third-party, and enterprise accounts.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.
